title: Cap. X Ultimum Propos. 1.III: Augustine — true grace is inspiration of love; he makes us walk and do; adjutorium whereby something is done; not only to be able but to will
pass_a_gloss: From Augustine we will taste a few things: Contra 2. Epist. Pelag. lib. 4. cap. 5. he thus describes true grace, The inspiration of love, that we may do what is known with holy love, is proper grace. And cap. 6. We walk, we observe, we do, but he makes that we walk, that we observe, that we do. This is the grace of God making us good, this his mercy preventing us. This grace of Christ he calls a help whereby something is done. He says that from this grace there is in us not only to be able to do what we will, but also to will what we can, De corr. et grat. cap. 11. and 12.
pass_b_english: A few from Augustine (Contra duas epistolas Pelagianorum 4.5): he describes true grace as the inspiration of love, that we may do what is known with holy love—that is proper grace. And 4.6: We walk, we keep, we do—but he makes us walk, keep, do. This is God’s grace making us good; this his mercy going before us. He calls this grace of Christ a help whereby something is done. From it, he says, there is in us not only power to do what we will, but also to will what we can (De correptione et gratia 11–12).
source_text: Ex Augustino paucula delibemus: Contra 2. Epist. Pelag. lib. 4. cap. 5. gratiam veram sic describit, Inspiratio dilectionis, ut cognita sancto amore faciamus, propria gratia est. Et cap. 6. Nos ambulamus, nos observamus, nos facimus, sed ille facit ut ambulemus, ut observemus, ut faciamus. Haec est gratia Dei bonos faciens nos, haec misericordia ejus praeveniens nos. Hanc gratiam Christi vocat adjutorium quo aliquid fit. Dicit ab hac gratia esse in nobis non solum posse quod volumus, verum etiam velle quod possumus, De corr. et grat. cap. 11. et 12.
